findings.text: The opening tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. They could repeat it after one paragraph.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The page explains why a site named Athena is mostly about a different project, firstmate: the study is a demonstration. Without this sentence, the title would confuse a newcomer.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim"

findings.text: The next step is concrete: clone, check the prerequisites, run setup.sh, then try a one-line request. A link near the top jumps to this section. It does not say which operating systems are supported, or whether the reader needs a paid model account or API key, even though the lede stresses cost.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: This link appears in the header and nothing explains it. A newcomer does not know who the "owner" is, or whether these proposals concern them.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Terms such as captain, yolo, green/red and worktree are defined before they are used, and a three-part "Start here" orients the reader. This makes the firstmate content readable for someone who knows neither project.
findings.source: Start here / "Words used first" and the Glossary

findings.text: Some cards pack several conditions into one long sentence and repeat the summary above them. A first-time reader will find these hard to scan.
findings.source: Transitions, t4 Guard: "worktree clean and committed work landed, whether the captain approved the merge, firstmate merged it under yolo, or a local-only ship landed by a guarded fast-forward; a local-only project also counts..."

findings.text: The claims list uses words the Glossary never defines, so a newcomer who checks a claim meets new jargon.
findings.source: Claims c3, c9, c37, c41: "brief", "endpoint", "heartbeat", "the main first mate", "crewmates"

findings.text: The page has no "concurrency entry". Card ra3 cites only c5 and c6, and c44 appears only under the Glossary entry for secondmate, so this cross-reference leads nowhere.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f2: "The page attaches those claims to the counter, to the relaunch transition, to the queued state and to the concurrency entry."

findings.text: The page says plainly that nothing was run and that every claim comes from reading files. That helps a newcomer judge how much to trust the study.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read"
